source.title: Rethinking Gauss-Newton for learning over-parameterized models
source.authors: M. Arbel; Romain Menegaux; Pierre Wolinski

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study empirically tests how network parameterization relates to test error in an over-parameterized regression task, using a width sweep rather than the settings named in V2. It also reports other optimizer and initialization effects on generalization that fit none of the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a width sweep with test error stable once the network can fit the data. Its GN-versus-GD and initialization results concern synthetic teacher-generated regression and are not tests of V4's adaptive optimizers or the other listed versions. Cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out loss as trained one-hidden-layer networks widen beyond sufficient capacity to interpolate. This tests V2 in a new setting: synthetic teacher/student regression with SiLU, mean-field output scaling, and full-batch GN or GD.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors distinguish their conditional global-convergence guarantee from generalization: small initialization and small GN step sizes can favor useful features, with slower optimization. An under-optimized final layer can obscure this feature quality in raw training and test loss, which linear refitting can reveal.
record.recipe_differences: Exact, deterministic, full-batch Gauss-Newton and gradient descent on one-hidden-layer synthetic regression networks; the width result is a parameterization sweep, not the original width experiments on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization varies with initialization standard deviation and step size; results also vary with activation choice. In Appendix C.3, which optimizer performs better depends on the SiLU temperature β.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-features test error improves as the number of fixed random features increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing random-feature capacity can improve minimum-norm regression generalization beyond interpolation.

fits_no_version.finding: Initialization scale controls whether GN and GD improve over random features; small initialization favors feature learning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale affects feature learning and generalization in over-parameterized teacher/student regression.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller GN step sizes yield better learned features and lower test loss after linear refitting, at the cost of slower optimization; GD shows the opposite step-size trend. Related behavior appears on teacher-generated MNIST targets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relation between step size, feature quality, and optimization speed depends on the optimizer.

record.problems: The main experiments use a synthetic teacher/student regression task and a single seed for the figures in the main text; the authors report five-run results in the appendix. Width-sweep values are presented in a figure, with the text describing the trend but not giving exact values. These results do not test random-label memorization or the listed image-classification settings.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows omitted. The initialization, step-size, and feature-quality findings are described under fits_no_version because none of the listed versions names those measurements or interventions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting compared with natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
The original ReLU image-classification settings on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10. The study does not establish an interpolation-threshold test-error peak.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adam or related adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other complexity measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V2. Its plateau challenges continued improvement only in the tested regression setting; it does not show that widening raises test error. The supplied figure text does not permit reliable numerical transcription of the width-sweep losses.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
One-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10; the reported width sweep uses a synthetic teacher/student task and includes SiLU.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks on image datasets.
Adaptive optimizers such as Adam compared with SGD or momentum SGD.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training–test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
